## Appendix D Repair Construction Details

#### Sources and identity.

Each confirmed failure is frozen together with its inspection record and
diagnosis and four trace streams: the requests sent to the model, the
agent’s outputs and tool calls, state persistence, and the content
rendered to the user. Cases are keyed by both case and conversation
identity, and file manifests are hashed. The persistence and rendering
streams support attribution but never enter the student input, and
neither do other cases from the same conversation, neighboring requests,
or a policy revision newer than the incident.

#### Anchors.

The first erroneous decision is anchored by the request identity
together with the exact logged output and its content hash. Ordinal
positions (“the third assistant turn”), the first occurrence of a
repeated request identity, and earlier repair artifacts are not accepted
as anchors, although earlier artifacts may help to locate a candidate
that is then re-verified against the frozen sources.

#### Verification axes.

Table [20](#A4.T20 "Table 20 ‣ Verification axes. ‣ Appendix D Repair Construction Details ‣ CARE: Grounded Recursive Self-Improvementfor Production Customer-Service Agents")
lists the axes of the independent verifier. A tuple is admitted only if
every axis takes its passing value; ineligible, unrepaired,
undetermined, malformed, and pending outcomes are all excluded.

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
| Axis |  Question | Passing value |
| Disposition |  Is the case repaired by the proposed decision? | repaired |
| Eligibility |  May the pair be used for training at all? | eligible |
| Fault relation |  Is the anchored output the model’s own fault? | model fault |
| Symptom |  Is the inspected symptom corrected? | corrected |
| Boundary |  Is the change confined to the anchored decision? | corrected |
| Policy |  Does the repair follow the incident-time SOP? | compliant |
| Format |  Does it respect the Skill, tool, and field contract? | compliant |

Table 20: Axes of the independent repair verifier.

#### Training admission.

A verified tuple is a candidate, not yet training data. Before the OPSD
runs of
Section [8](#S8 "8 Experiments ‣ CARE: Grounded Recursive Self-Improvementfor Production Customer-Service Agents"),
every selected tuple passed the following checks: (i) *request
fidelity*: the student messages equal the frozen request and its content
hash matches, with tools retained and the prompt ending where the next
assistant turn begins; (ii) *privilege isolation*: the teacher text is
non-empty and absent from the student request, verified by reading every
tuple back through the actual training dataset and collator; (iii)
*visual evidence*: every image resolves to a frozen file whose hash,
size, and decoding are checked, and tuples with more than four images
are excluded whole; (iv) *length*: student and teacher contexts are
encoded with the target tokenizer, chat template, tool schemas, and
image processor, and must fit the 32K context together with a
2,048-token response budget, with truncation treated as an error; and
(v) a one-step run on the full training layout, covering rollout,
teacher scoring, update, checkpointing, export, and independent
readback, after which training restarts from the initial checkpoint.
Replaying the incident model at $`x`$, to test whether the original
error reproduces, is a separate check.

## Appendix E OPSD Training Configuration

Table [21](#A5.T21 "Table 21 ‣ Appendix E OPSD Training Configuration ‣ CARE: Grounded Recursive Self-Improvementfor Production Customer-Service Agents")
lists the OPSD configuration of the final model (configuration 4 of
Table [10](#S8.T10 "Table 10 ‣ 8.7 Ablation: OPSD loss ‣ 8 Experiments ‣ CARE: Grounded Recursive Self-Improvementfor Production Customer-Service Agents")).
Configurations 1, 2, and 3 of
Section [8.7](#S8.SS7 "8.7 Ablation: OPSD loss ‣ 8 Experiments ‣ CARE: Grounded Recursive Self-Improvementfor Production Customer-Service Agents")
share every setting except the objective row, which
Table [10](#S8.T10 "Table 10 ‣ 8.7 Ablation: OPSD loss ‣ 8 Experiments ‣ CARE: Grounded Recursive Self-Improvementfor Production Customer-Service Agents")
gives for each of them. SFT and DPO in
Section [8.6](#S8.SS6 "8.6 Ablation: how to learn from verified repairs ‣ 8 Experiments ‣ CARE: Grounded Recursive Self-Improvementfor Production Customer-Service Agents")
use the same initialization, repair tuples, and training budget.

|  |  |
|----|----|
|  Item |  Setting |
|  Student initialization |  V4, the previous version; full-parameter update, vision tower trainable |
|  Teacher |  V4, frozen for the whole run, not a moving average; scores the student’s rollout token by token; targets detached and kept in FP32 |
|  Privileged information |  appended to the teacher’s system message; never in the student context |
|  Training set |  280 repair tuples after micro-scenario capping (Section [6.3](#S6.SS3 "6.3 Data selection and mixing across policy versions ‣ 6 Phase II: Evolve by Attribution-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation ‣ CARE: Grounded Recursive Self-Improvementfor Production Customer-Service Agents")); 281 candidates, one excluded for exceeding four images per tuple |
|  Objective |  forward KL partial sum over the teacher’s top 32 tokens, floored at zero per token (Eq. [29](#S6.E29 "In A family of truncated KL losses. ‣ 6.2 Hindsight as privileged information ‣ 6 Phase II: Evolve by Attribution-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation ‣ CARE: Grounded Recursive Self-Improvementfor Production Customer-Service Agents")); backpropagated directly; loss coefficient 1.0; mean over all generated tokens of the batch (Eq. [31](#S6.E31 "In A family of truncated KL losses. ‣ 6.2 Hindsight as privileged information ‣ 6 Phase II: Evolve by Attribution-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation ‣ CARE: Grounded Recursive Self-Improvementfor Production Customer-Service Agents")) |
|  Not used |  task reward, policy gradient, tail cell, renormalization within the top-$`K`$ set, probability floor or smoothing, auxiliary SFT or DPO loss |
|  Student sampling |  one sample per tuple and update; temperature 1.0, top-$`p`$ 1.0, no top-$`k`$; single turn; at most 2,048 response tokens |
|  Context limits |  prompt $`\leq`$ 30,719 tokens; prompt plus response $`\leq`$ 32,768 tokens for both student and teacher contexts; no truncation |
|  Optimizer |  AdamW, $`\beta=(0.9,0.999)`$, weight decay 0.01, gradient-norm clipping 1.0, fresh state |
|  Learning rate |  peak $`5\times 10^{-6}`$, linear warmup over 5% of steps (10 steps), cosine decay |
|  Batch and schedule |  global batch 4, three epochs of 70 steps; 210 steps; the third epoch is the final model |
|  Precision and parallelism |  BF16; 16 GPUs, sequence parallel 8 $`\times`$ data parallel 2, one sequence per micro-batch |
|  Checkpoints |  end of every epoch; each exported and independently read back |

Table 21: OPSD training configuration of the final model.
